title: [Crop And Lock] T mode thumbnail turns black/blank when another application enters fullscreen mode

judgment.rationale: The report isolates black content to the cropped browser video while the thumbnail window stays visible; DWM video-surface availability is a stronger investigation boundary than window topmost placement.
evidence: PowerToys 0.102.3101 on Windows build 26300, non-elevated per-machine installation, with screenshots and an existing diagnostic ZIP.
Edge video crops become black when another app enters fullscreen; audio continues and Alt+Tab restores the thumbnail.
Cropping the browser address bar works under the same conditions; the report also mentions Chrome 157.
Current ThumbnailCropAndLockWindow.cpp registers a DWM thumbnail with DwmRegisterThumbnail and sets its source crop/visibility with DwmUpdateThumbnailProperties.
No direct #52143 PR was found. The video-versus-address-bar control suggests a browser/compositor surface interaction, not proof of a Crop and Lock repaint defect.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce video versus nonvideo crops with browser acceleration and fullscreen modes varied before deciding whether a capture fallback is needed.

proposed_fixes.title: Handle unavailable video surfaces in thumbnail capture
proposed_fixes.root_cause: DWM thumbnails may lose a hardware video surface under fullscreen occlusion; the working address-bar crop and Alt+Tab recovery fit this hypothesis but do not prove the responsible layer.
plan: Run the supplied crop/control matrix and determine whether DWM loses only hardware video planes.
If the surface is unavailable to DWM, evaluate a scoped supported capture fallback or an actionable limitation message rather than repeated thumbnail recreation.
Retain source-window crop, scaling and lifecycle behavior and avoid promising capture of protected video.
verification: Check hardware-accelerated/nonaccelerated browser video, fullscreen transitions and address-bar controls; verify no hidden/minimized-source regression.

confidence.rationale: The source boundary and controls are specific, but GPU/browser/compositor behavior and fallback feasibility are unmeasured.

actions.label: Approve Handle unavailable video surfaces in thumbnail capture

reproduce.title: Verify reported Crop and Lock behavior
prerequisites: A browser with a public nonprotected test video and a second application supporting fullscreen.
steps: In Edge play a nonprotected public test video, then crop its player using Win+Ctrl+Shift+T.
Keep Edge unminimized and enter fullscreen in another application; observe thumbnail content and audio.
Alt+Tab back and repeat with a crop of the address bar.
Repeat with browser hardware acceleration disabled after restarting the browser, and compare borderless versus exclusive fullscreen where available.
reproduce.expected_result: The thumbnail continues to show capturable source content; any compositor/video-surface limitation is isolated and documented.
